title: Twist7 torsion to rational elliptic isogeny quotients: explicit maps and charged solver test
status_note: Concrete follow-up proposal after verified generator-order/construction evidence. Not implemented or run; no protocol/source freeze or resource estimate. No funding/lease/allocation. Existing full-campaign criteria are unchanged.
blocked_on: note:Implement native instruments, independent certificate/replay, measured sizing and pre-data protocol before readiness.
question: Can the p827 twist7-torsion structure supply explicitly certified rational7-isogeny quotients of the source with cheaper complete decomposition?
decision_value: An executable scalar-preserving map to another same-order elliptic curve would establish that connection; only a charged destination-solving gain establishes a speedup. Standard isogeny theory is not a novelty claim.

resources.notes: Start only with public icv1-fp10-t5-192cb216 and its registered twist, whose independent group structure is C7 x C119. First certify a basis of actual twist7-torsion and its anti-Frobenius embedding in source E[7]. Enumerate the eight cyclic kernel lines; verify Galois stability before claiming rational quotients. Construct all8 degree7 Velu maps, model identities and duals, including poles/infinity. Independently check curve cardinalities, kernel, subgroup preservation, G and public37G transport, and recovery via dual/inverse7 mod823. No NIST DLP. Register exact curve/map identities. Only then freeze same-base source/destination solver and ordinary group controls, charging map discovery, target conversion, roots/signs, useful rows and recovery. Proposed map-search600s/4GiB envelope is unmeasured, not funding. Full estimates remain missing; nominal resource fields do not authorize a launch.

outputs.result_schema: Proposed only. All8 kernels and maps independently certified with exact cleared-polynomial identities and source/target checks; a genuine generator/target scalar transport with all exceptional cases covered. A separate frozen full-cost panel must beat the strongest existing solver on the same output task to claim a solver gain. A Frobenius factor, group-order match, known-scalar multiplication or given-map toy transport alone does not establish IC improvement.
